title: Added workflow file for validating pnpm-lock file
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary
This PR adds a GitHub Action workflow to enforce best practices around the pnpm-lock.yaml file. It includes the following automated checks on every pull request:

✅ What it validates:
No tarball: fields in pnpm-lock.yaml

- Prevents local or non-registry tarball references that break reproducibility.
- No packages/mermaid/src/vitepress paths in the lockfile
- Ensures build-only or dev-only paths are not accidentally locked.
- No lockfile changes without corresponding package.json changes
- Guards against unintended lockfile commits that are not tied to real dependency updates.

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html)
- [ ] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation. Make sure [`MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION`](https://mermaid.js.org/community/contributing.html#update-documentation) is used for all new features.
- [x] :butterfly: If your PR makes a change that should be noted in one or more packages' changelogs, generate a changeset by running `pnpm changeset` and following the prompts. Changesets that add features should be `minor` and those that fix bugs should be `patch`. Please prefix changeset messages with `feat:`, `fix:`, or `chore:`.
author: shubhamparikh2704

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Please remove changeset, this is not a change that requires a mermaid release.
comments.label_reasoning: The changeset file is unnecessary/redundant for this type of change and should be removed — it's an unused artifact.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Explicitly requests removal of the changeset file.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: We should specify what the error is.
comments.label_reasoning: The comment asks for a clearer error message to be specified, indicating the current description/output lacks clarity.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests that the error message be made more specific, implying a code change.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Why do we need the `'**/*.js'` selector?
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer is questioning whether the '**/*.js' selector is necessary, implying it may be redundant or unnecessary in the workflow trigger.

comments.author: shubhamparikh2704
comments.body: If the PR touches source code (e.g. adds a new import in a .js file) and  forgotten to bump package.json and regenerate pnpm-lock.yaml, the validation step will still fire the workflow. But it was not necessary. Can be removed.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Questions the need for the selector, implying it should be removed or justified — a suggestion disguised as a question.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
```suggestion
            issues+=("• Disallowed path 'packages/mermaid/src/vitepress' present. Run `rm -rf packages/mermaid/src/vitepress && pnpm install` to regenerate.")
```
comments.label_reasoning: The suggestion improves the error message to be more descriptive and actionable, indicating the original lacked sufficient clarity about the issue and remediation steps.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a direct code suggestion to replace an existing line with a more descriptive error message.
